fact_text: The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator whose reading moves only between 0 and 100 and is applied to the price chart of the KSE-100 index.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)

fact_text: The default RSI input length and smoothing length are both 14 periods, and the analyst advises leaving them unchanged.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)

fact_text: An RSI reading above 70 is the overbought zone, meaning buying in the stock has been heavy.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)

fact_text: An RSI reading below 30 is the oversold zone, meaning selling has been heavy.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)

fact_text: The analyst expects a correction after RSI rises above 70, and a possible reversal once RSI falls below 30.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)

fact_text: The analyst treats RSI as a momentum indicator: a rising RSI suggests the trend can extend upward, while an RSI below 30 signals bearish momentum.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)

fact_text: The analyst views an RSI below 30 as bearish momentum, so he does not treat it as a buying signal at that point.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, '9. How to Use RSI (Relative Strength Index) in Technical Analysis | Live KSE 100 Index Analysis' (YouTube, 2024-10-13)
